newsitem.title: GERMANY: Intel - no reason for weak European demand.
newsitem.headline: Intel - no reason for weak European demand.

text.p: Computer Chip maker Intel Corp. said on Monday it did not know why demand in Europe had unexpectedly softened and that it saw no signs competitors were gaining market share in the region.
"We don't know why (demand is weak), either," Intel spokesman Heiner Genzken told Reuters. "We see no signs (competitors) are winning market share."

Intel shares on Friday tumbled more than $12 to $151.50 after the company said weak demand, especially in Europe, would cause second-quarter sales to come in five to 10 percent below the first-quarter total of $6.4 billion.
Rivals Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Cyrix Corp. recently released new chips that compete with Intel's fastest processors, and have won some customers in Europe.
Fujitsu's PC business, which has a 3.7 percent market share in Europe, and Vobis Microcomputer AG, one of Germany's largest PC makers, have agreed to use AMd's K6 processor.
Genzken said demand was strong for Intel's fastest chips -- the Pentium II and Pentium with MMX multimedia capabilities. "Demand is greater than we can deliver," he said.
But demand for standard Pentium chips was "very weak," he said.
Intel does not break out its sales mix by products, Genzken said. He also declined to say what countries were showing weakest demand.
